job.title: Security Engineer, Offensive Security
job.pay_full: US Zone 2: $193,500 – $261,900 a year; US Zone 3: $172,000 – $232,800 a year (not available in US Zone 1)

details.about: Within Dropbox Security, this Offensive Security Engineer investigates how attackers could compromise Dropbox's products and infrastructure, including AI-enabled applications and agentic systems. It is a hands-on offensive security and threat research role: you contribute to investigations and multi-phase red team exercises, develop attack techniques and build tooling, working with Product Security, Detection & Response, Threat Intelligence, Privacy and engineering teams.
duties: Plan and run offensive security assessments, setting objectives, scope, rules of engagement and safeguards
Investigate unfamiliar applications, infrastructure, APIs and trust boundaries to trace meaningful attack paths
Develop and safely demonstrate exploits and attack chains that show potential impact
Build and improve offensive security tools, agents, automation and testing harnesses
Assess security risks across AI-enabled applications, agents, tool integrations and supporting infrastructure
Work with security, privacy, legal and engineering teams to communicate risk, fix root causes and verify improvements through retesting
needs: 5+ years in offensive security, vulnerability research, red teaming or closely related security engineering, or equivalent demonstrated capability
A track record of independently leading complex investigations or engagements and finding and exploiting non-trivial vulnerabilities
Understanding of application security, authentication and authorization, cloud infrastructure, APIs and software supply chains, with deep expertise in one or more
Hands-on experience attacking or evaluating LLMs, AI agents, ML systems, AI-enabled applications or agentic architectures
Familiarity with security risks in AI-enabled applications, agents and tool integrations
Ability to write code to build or adapt offensive tools and automation, and to read unfamiliar production codebases
nice: Developing novel attacks or repeatable security evaluations for AI-enabled systems
Expertise across several attack surfaces, or specialist skill in exploit development, reverse engineering, endpoint security, cloud exploitation or supply-chain attacks
Automated vulnerability discovery, fuzzing or program analysis
Coordinated exercises with defenders to measure detection and response
Original research, vulnerability disclosures, open-source tools, publications or mentoring
details.benefits: Base pay by US zone: Zone 2 $193,500 – $261,900 a year; Zone 3 $172,000 – $232,800 a year. The role is not available in US Zone 1.
notes: Teams with on-call rotations expect all engineers to take part, including outside core business hours
